beats.headline: Ten hands at Chaco's counter
beats.text: Over chat, Mordecai wants to know whether the prize counter has any sheet music like Chaco's own escape spell. Chaco looks up in surprise: Carl has a bard in his party? Can she hold pitch? He points at a sheet at ten hands, a song of Skedaddle, not quite as good as Wings of the Pyxie, which she could not sing for a while anyway. Sheet music sits somewhere between a scroll and a magic book. With it in front of her, the system helps a bard perform; sung badly the page tears a little, too many tears and it is ruined, and sung perfectly the song joins her repertoire. Carl adds it to his order.

beats.headline: Handy, in case of swarm
beats.text: Sister Ines wants to march straight into a fenced cemetery, and when Paz asks what if they get locked in, Donut points out that of course they will be: that is the whole purpose of the giant gate and fence. Once the nun agrees to circle the outside first, Carl tells Donut to keep the Skedaddle sheet music handy, and Puddle Jumper too. She already has, she says, but neither will let her leave if they are locked in. The place is big, Carl answers. Inside, they can use both to get away from a swarm, and with Skedaddle they can jump twice, as long as she sings it in key. What is that supposed to mean, Donut asks, when he called her masquerade performance flawless?

beats.headline: Not into Sheol fire
beats.text: Imani and Tran are trapped in a pocket below, Elle and the others are digging desperately through the rubble, and demons are coming up from both sides. Carl needs Donut to get rid of her deck, and asks whether she still has Puddle Jump available, to get everybody out. She still has Skedaddle as well, but Carl leaves that one alone: the escape spell would likely dump them all into a pile of Sheol fire.
